<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ExecutionContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 066177b80fd6a444e3fc44a23cb6b818d2407399` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b13c4f046c6854a5bc3ca41e5fb59f6783a386f` — the merge of head `24233e955c33ee77052d41ad1e7acdadc37f2368` into base `066177b80fd6a444e3fc44a23cb6b818d2407399`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b13c4f046c6854a5bc3ca41e5fb59f6783a386f && git checkout 8b13c4f046c6854a5bc3ca41e5fb59f6783a386f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 066177b80fd6a444e3fc44a23cb6b818d2407399 24233e955c33ee77052d41ad1e7acdadc37f2368 && git checkout -B drift-repro 066177b80fd6a444e3fc44a23cb6b818d2407399 && git merge --no-ff 24233e955c33ee77052d41ad1e7acdadc37f2368

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 066177b80fd6a444e3fc44a23cb6b818d2407399
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 066177b80fd6a444e3fc44a23cb6b818d2407399` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · card #33694 · area o2-B · first review · read at 2026-11-17T01:09Z
Head-sha: `768136c0ef3a8d15683477fed1f62bb2b4c8b72f` (the final head announced in comment 6934548662)

Checklist, read against GitHub and the head tree, not against the report:

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`. The first card line is `Fixes #33694`, and it is the only closing keyword in the body. `Fixes` is right: the card is the plugin-audit writer half after the split (6893182618), and its blocker #33786 is closed. The remaining writers and the doc table are carried by #34556, which is open, `pm:blocked`, Blocked-by #33694, and enumerates all four items.
- **File surface** (`get_files`, 8 files, +243/-33). `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`, its integration test, and the describe and JSDoc in `packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`. Three regenerated `content/docs/references/**` pages, consistent with `check:generated`, which `Lint & Repo Gates` carries and which passed. The changeset. This matches the claim's surface (6932852581). No `content/docs/releases/` change.
- **Fix, read in the diff.**
  - One reader, `provenanceMark` (non-blank trimmed string, else absent), now serves all four `provenance.performedBy*` keys. The old `performedByClientId` read moved onto it unchanged.
  - `performedBy = performedByClientId ?? performedByAgentId`. The /mcp door and the in-product path each stamp only their own key, and `ExecutionContext.performedBy` refines to at least one of the two.
  - `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id` are read only when a performer is present, and are written only beside `performed_by`. A personal write still reaches no `metadata` (the guard is `performedBy || impersonatedBy || signInStamp || scimConnectionId`).
  - `user_id` and `actor` are not touched (ADR-0118 D1/D5).
  - At the head, `audit-writers.ts` holds exactly one performer read (`:2206–2225`) and one stamp (`:2380–2387`). No other record-write path in the file reads `performedByClientId` alone.
  - The other plugin-audit writers that read `performedBy.clientId` only are the three named in #34556. The spec describes now say so.
- **Ruling and names.** The owner ruling on objectstack-ai/cloud#3826 (「3826 照建议（征询版）」) chose the existing `performed_by` / `on_behalf_of` pair and no new actor vocabulary, and the code follows it. The two new metadata keys `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id` are the seat's call per the area note: snake_case, beside `performed_by` / `on_behalf_of` / `impersonated_by`.
  - The dev flags that `performed_by` now holds two id namespaces, an OAuth client id or an agent name. That follows the ruling. The contract reviewer gets it as a review point, and #34057 carries the ADR note. It does not block L1.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch (behaviour: new keys on audit rows) and `@objectstack/spec` patch (describe text ships). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in both the body and the changeset; the accept sets are unchanged and no schema shape moves. `Skills-docs:` is not owed. I checked its prose sentence by sentence against the diff:
  - "the record-write audit writer read only the OAuth client (`performedByClientId`)": true at the merge-base.
  - The three bullets match the stamp at `:2385–2387`, including that the confirmation key is present only when stamped.
  - "`user_id` and `actor` still name the person": untouched.
  - "The action-invocation, data-export and dataset-query rows still record the OAuth client only": true, and carried by #34556.
- **Tests.** New describe, 4 cases, in the existing real-kernel harness: `assembleExecutionContext`, objectql `buildProvenance`, the shipped `sys_audit_log` on sqlite-wasm.
  - CONTROL: a `human` principal with no `performedBy`, and `user_id` / `actor` is the person on every row.
  - The confirmed AI write, the unconfirmed AI write, and the AI update after a personal create each pin the whole `metadata` object with `toEqual`, so a stray key fails. The personal create row's `metadata` is null.
  - Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, `?? performedByAgentId` removed): 3 failed / 10 passed, exactly the three AI rows; restored blob == HEAD.
  - No existing test changed.
- **Boundary.** The cloud in-product AI path that stamps `performedBy.agentId` lives outside this repository. The test adds `performedBy` to a door-built envelope the way that path stamps it. The value travels through the real `buildProvenance` and the shipped writer, so the in-repo boundary is exercised end to end.
- **Gates (check-runs at `768136c0`, `filter=latest`, 72 runs).** 60 `success`, 12 path-filtered `skipped`, none red or pending. Required floor: Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`. `Test Core` aggregate `success`, shards 1–8/8 `success`. Also `success`: Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate). Local `dispatch-gates --ran`: 119/119, 0 NOT-MEASURED. That is a local subset only; the check-runs are the reading I used.
- **Out of scope.** Both report findings have a destination: the three non-record writers and `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx:120` are enumerated on #34556.

**L2 owed: yes, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** `packages/spec/src/**` (non-test) describes are touched. At this reading there is a claim (6934565857, l2-review#4, head `768136c0`) and no record yet. With no same-form PASS at this head, the dispatching area adds `needs:contract-review` to the PR with this ACCEPT. The `performed_by` two-namespace point is the review's to judge.

**Landing tier.** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34547` reads: "0 of 8 path(s) hit the register … ✅ NOT governed — ordinary queue landing applies"; 276 changed lines ≤ 3000. The area lands it through the ordinary queue once the L2 PASS is recorded on this same head and every check is green.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `768136c0ef3a8d15683477fed1f62bb2b4c8b72f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #33694 (body and all 5 comments), PR #34547 (body, 8-file list, net diff against merge-base 0c7869c0, comments), and the 72 check-runs on this head: every one is completed, success or skipped by path filter, none red and none pending.

- Accept set of `ExecutionContextSchema.performedBy` and `HookContextSchema.provenance`: unchanged. The diff edits describe strings and JSDoc only; no key, type, refine or optionality moves. Right.
- Published surface of `@objectstack/spec`: four describe strings change (`performedBy`, `provenance.performedByAgentId`, `performedByConversationId`, `performedByConfirmationId`), and through them `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx`, `data/data-engine.mdx` (12 rows) and `kernel/execution-context.mdx`. The generated rows carry the new describe text verbatim; no stale "does not record them yet" sentence is left anywhere in the head tree. Right.
- Public behaviour of `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: a record-write `sys_audit_log` row whose provenance carries `performedByAgentId` now gets `metadata.performed_by` (the agent) and `on_behalf_of` (the person), plus `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id` when stamped. Additive metadata keys; `user_id` and `actor` do not move; a row with no performer is byte-identical to before (the metadata guard is the same disjunction with `performedBy` in place of `performedByClientId`, and `performedBy` equals `performedByClientId` whenever no agent id is present). Right.
- The OAuth client path: `provenanceMark` is the same non-blank-string-trimmed read the inline expression made; an OAuth client row is unchanged unless its envelope also carried a conversation or confirmation id, which no producer in the tree sets (`tool-call-interceptor.ts:116` freezes the client id alone). Right.
- `metadata.performed_by` on the record-write row now holds two id kinds (a `sys_oauth_application` id, or an in-product agent name). This is what the owner ruling on cloud#3826, as quoted on the card, chose ("using the existing `performed_by` / `on_behalf_of` columns ... Do not add a new actor vocabulary"). Right as ruled; how the contract tells a reader about it is S1 under ④.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/33694-audit-in-product-ai-performer.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. Both packages the diff moves are named and no other released package is moved. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (nothing a metadata author can write changes), and `none` takes patch. `Clause-②: no` is right: no accept set changes, and the line is present and identical in the PR body and the changeset. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag and `open_questions` 1 (two id namespaces in `performed_by`; accept as ruled, or ask for a discriminator): answered. Accept the shared key as ruled (option A); no new key and no decision card is needed. But option A's own premise, "a reader tells the in-product row by `conversation_id` when stamped", is written nowhere in the contract and is not guaranteed by it. That is S1 below, fixable in describe text.
- `open_questions` 2 (key names `conversation_id` / `confirmation_id`): answered, option A. Snake case beside `performed_by`, `on_behalf_of`, `impersonated_by`; the names mirror the contract fields; the seat approved them in PR comment 6934548662.
- Out-of-scope finding (action-invocation, data-export and dataset-query writers read `performedBy.clientId` only): confirmed in the head tree (`action-invocation-audit.ts:159`, `data-export-audit.ts:317`, `dataset-query-audit.ts:205`). The new describes state this limit truthfully, and the PR body names #34556 as its carrier. Accepted as a follow-up.
- Out-of-scope finding (`content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx:120` lists `performedByClientId` only): outside the diff, same carrier. Accepted as a follow-up.
- ADR bookkeeping: ADR-0090 D10 rule 4 on the head tree still reads "every write by an agent principal" and "a caller of any other kind ... the missing `performed_by` is itself the record that the principal acted for itself", while this writer now records `performed_by` on a `human` principal's row. The spec JSDoc already names the ADR note as the ruling's bookkeeping and the PR body names carrier #34057. Not this PR's file surface; noted so the carrier is not lost.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, against the ruling as quoted on the card, ADR-0151 D5 on the head tree, and the first consumer (`audit-writers.ts`):

S1 (should-fix) — the contract does not tell a reader of `sys_audit_log.metadata.performed_by` how to tell an OAuth client id from an in-product agent name. The `performedBy` describe says the writer "records the performer (clientId, or agentId for the in-product AI) as sys_audit_log.metadata.performed_by", the `performedByAgentId` describe says it is recorded "as `performed_by` beside `on_behalf_of`" exactly like the client id, and the three generated pages repeat both; none says how the two kinds are distinguished on the row. Three things make this more than wording:
  1. ADR-0151 D5 reason 2, accepted on main, refuses a second id kind in this key because it "gives one key two id namespaces, which a reader cannot tell apart". The ruling overrides the refusal for the in-product agent, but the stated harm stays unanswered in the text.
  2. The same JSDoc in `execution-context.zod.ts` still opens with "each naming its performer in its own key so one key never holds two id namespaces" (true of the envelope), and a few paragraphs later now says both keys land in one audit key, with no sentence joining the two.
  3. The only tell the dev names, `conversation_id`, is not a discriminator the contract backs: `conversationId` is optional in the schema, so an in-product row without it has exactly the shape of an OAuth client row; and the writer keys `conversation_id` / `confirmation_id` on any performer, so it would also write them beside a client id.
  The card's purpose is that the ledger answers "the AI changed this for this person in this conversation"; a row a reader cannot classify does not answer it. Fix on the describe face, no new key: state in the `performedBy` describe and JSDoc, and in the `performedByAgentId` describe, that the key holds either kind and how a reader resolves it (for example: a value that resolves as a registered `sys_oauth_application` id is the OAuth client, any other value is an in-product agent name; `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id` are written by the in-product path only), then regenerate. If the sentence names `conversation_id` / `confirmation_id` as in-product only, the writer must make it true by keying the two on the agent being the recorded performer (see N1). The fix moves the head and earns a delta review.

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`, sentence by sentence against the describes:

- "records the performer (clientId, or agentId for the in-product AI) as `performed_by` beside `on_behalf_of`": agrees (`performedByClientId ?? performedByAgentId`, `on_behalf_of: userId ?? null`, and `userId` is the person on the in-product path).
- "with conversationId as `metadata.conversation_id` and confirmationId as `metadata.confirmation_id` when set", and "beside `performed_by`": agrees; both are read only when a performer is recorded, and each key is spread only when non-blank.
- "the action-invocation, data-export and dataset-query rows record clientId only": agrees with the three writers in the head tree; no other writer in `packages/` sets `performed_by`.
- "It does not move `actor`": agrees; the diff touches neither `actor` nor `user_id`, and the CONTROL test pins both to the person on all four rows.
- "Absent on every write the person made themselves": agrees; the person's own create row keeps a null `metadata`, pinned by the fourth new test.
- The provenance chain (`buildProvenance` in `engine-execution-plumbing.ts`) already copies all four keys on the head tree, so the writer's reads are reachable; read, not reviewed.

N1 (nit) — when one envelope carries both `clientId` and `agentId` (the schema's refine permits it: "at least one of"), the writer records the client in `performed_by`, drops the agent name silently, and still writes the agent's `conversation_id` / `confirmation_id` beside the client id. The describes do not state this precedence; only a code comment does. No producer in the tree sets both, so it is unreachable today. Left as an accepted deviation unless the S1 fix touches the same lines, in which case gating the two keys on the agent being the recorded performer closes both.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1) is open on this head; landing waits on its fix and the delta record.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**L1 delta (patch round 2): ACCEPT** · PR #34547 · card #33694 · area o2-B · L1-a2 · 2026-11-17T02:19Z

Head-sha: `8cc21923d17bc4def8f92b936a87a51091d40090`

Previous L1: ACCEPT 6934586781 at `768136c0`. This record reads only the delta `768136c0..8cc21923`.

### What moved (read in git, not from the report)

- `0f655efa`: the fix (4 files, +66/−21).
- `0b288d13`: merge of `origin/main`. `git show --remerge-diff` is empty, so the merge is clean with no hand edits.
- `8cc21923`: regenerated `content/docs/references/{data/data-engine,data/hook,kernel/execution-context}.mdx` (+16/−16). These are table rows only, and each one mirrors the new describe text.

### Delta checklist

- **Writer** (`audit-writers.ts`): `agentIsRecordedPerformer = !performedByClientId && performedByAgentId !== undefined`. It now gates `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id`, which before were gated on any `performedBy`. `performed_by` is still `clientId ?? agentId`. `provenanceMark` already returns `undefined` for blank or non-string values, so `!performedByClientId` and `??` agree. This closes N1 and makes S1's "only beside the agent" sentence true.
- **Spec describes** (`execution-context.zod.ts` JSDoc and `.describe`, `hook.zod.ts` JSDoc and the three `performedBy*` describes): each one says that `performed_by` holds either kind, that a value matching the `client_id` of a registered `sys_oauth_application` row is the OAuth client and any other value is an agent name, that the two marks appear only beside the agent and their absence does not mark a client row, and that a both-performers envelope is recorded as the client. I checked the resolution key against the producer: `assemble-execution-context.ts:380` stamps `clientId` from the token's `azp`, which is the application's `client_id` column (`sys-oauth-application.object.ts`). So `client_id` is the right column to name. No key added, no shape change.
- **Tests**: 2 new pins in `agent-dual-attribution.integration.test.ts` (client beside stray marks → pair only; both performers → client only, no marks). The ablation log `33694-ablation-r2.log` reads `Tests 2 failed | 13 passed (15)` with the gate swapped back to `performedBy !== undefined`, then `ok restored: blob == HEAD (cc64d3be6bc7)`. Both pins are live.
- **Changeset** (`.changeset/33694-audit-in-product-ai-performer.md`, unchanged this round): re-read against the new behaviour. Its bullets list `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id` as the in-product AI's marks and say nothing about them riding beside a client, so they are still true.
- **PR body**: first line `Fixes #33694`, the only closing keyword in the body. Round 2 is described under Spec describes and in the namespaces note.
- **CI on this head** (check-runs, `filter=latest`, 72 runs): `success=60`, `skipped=12`, nothing red or pending.

### Nit, not blocking (for the L2 delta to weigh)

The `performedByClientId` describe in `hook.zod.ts`, a line this round did not touch, still calls the value "a registered sys_oauth_application id". The new sentences beside it say `client_id`. These read as the same thing only to a reader who knows `azp` is the `client_id`. Not filed.
